name: Roll from Chill Dog
summary: A safe reset from Chill Dog opens the high-leg control before any change of facing direction; the position does not itself require a rolling turtle escape.
description: A safe reset from Chill Dog opens the high-leg control before any change of facing direction; the position does not itself require a rolling turtle escape.
overview:
The bottom player is already facing the opponent in Chill Dog, with a high rubber-guard leg connection. No direct roll from the named high-guard configuration was established by the reviewed instruction. Do not roll onto the neck while retaining a loaded shoulder connection.

The bottom player is on the back or hip with a high rubber-guard leg across the upper back. One of the top player's arms is isolated beside the bottom player rather than framing inside. Release any wrist, neck or elbow loading before opening the high-leg enclosure. Lower the controlling leg through a comfortable hip angle rather than pulling the foot against the knee.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Brandon McCaghren — Gogoplata from rubber guard](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wn39-wrfsbs); [Eddie Bravo — Chill Dog / Invisible Collar clarification](https://www.10thplanetjj.com/forum/threads/17657-Chill-Dog-Invisible-Collar-Question).

flashcards.question: Roll from Chill Dog (bottom): What relationship exists before this proposed roll?
flashcards.answer: Chill Dog begins with the bottom player facing the opponent in a neck-cleared high guard, not underneath a rear ride.

plausible: Mission Control, both arms inside
Closed guard, both legs low at waist

flashcards.question: Roll from Chill Dog (bottom): What must open before changing the facing direction?
flashcards.answer: Release neck and shoulder tension before changing direction so a turn does not carry a captured joint through rotation.

plausible: Only free foot; arm remains fixed
Only mat post; neck loop stays tight

flashcards.question: Roll from Chill Dog (bottom): How should the high leg lower for a reset?
flashcards.answer: Open the connection and move the hip so the leg lowers through available space without dragging the ankle across the knee.
flashcards.answer_line: Move hip with high knee supported

plausible: Hold knee still and haul the foot
Straighten into their shoulder
trap: Flatten hip before foot grip opens

flashcards.question: Roll from Chill Dog (bottom): What should replace the high-leg connection?
flashcards.answer: Restore a facing guard barrier after release instead of leaving both legs outside while the opponent advances.
flashcards.answer_line: Inside forearms and knees bar torso

plausible: Hands clasped behind their head
Both knees drawn behind you

flashcards.question: Roll from Chill Dog (bottom): Which movement creates knee room after release?
flashcards.answer: The supported hip escape creates room for a knee after the high connection opens; it does not require a somersault.
flashcards.answer_line: Short hip escape behind the frame

plausible: Roll backward with high leg attached
Sit straight into the opposing chest
trap: Slide hips after dropping the frame

flashcards.question: Roll from Chill Dog (bottom): What can happen if you roll with their arm still fixed?
flashcards.answer: A torso turn can load a shoulder that remains fixed by the knee hug. Release that arm before any separately established roll.
flashcards.answer_line: Torso turns around a fixed shoulder

plausible: Upper arm slips out as hips turn
Head grip opens before arm loads
trap: Clamped elbow follows the torso turn

flashcards.question: Roll from Chill Dog (bottom): Where should the forearm frame sit while your inside knee returns?
flashcards.answer: Keep the forearm inside the approaching shoulder while the hips make knee room. This barrier keeps the passer from filling the recovery gap with a crossface and chest control.

plausible: Outside their approaching upper arm
Low at belt as shoulder crosses face

flashcards.question: Roll from Chill Dog (bottom): Why does a free hand alone not authorize a roll?
flashcards.answer: Check the actual upper-body enclosure; hand freedom does not establish that captured joints can rotate safely.
flashcards.answer_line: Leg may still fix shoulder or neck

plausible: Hand moves, so elbow can follow turn
Free leg lowered, so head loop opens

flashcards.question: Roll from Chill Dog (bottom): Your neck takes weight during the turn; what now?
flashcards.answer: Do not continue a turn that transfers weight onto the neck; unload and reopen the high connection before recovery.

plausible: Finish roll before lowering high leg
Pull them tighter for more momentum
trap: Pause hips but keep high-leg tension

flashcards.question: Roll from Chill Dog (bottom): What verifies the supported reset at the end?
flashcards.answer: The documented recovery checkpoint is the restored guard barrier after the high connection opens, not a guaranteed rolling destination.
flashcards.answer_line: Facing guard, knee and forearm in

plausible: Roll done, both knees still outside
Overhook kept while chest is pinned

flashcards.question: Roll from Chill Dog (top): How should you protect the isolated arm as they shift?
flashcards.answer: Preserve inside space with the free arm and avoid letting the isolated elbow drift farther from your torso.
flashcards.answer_line: Compact elbow, free arm frames in

plausible: Flare caught elbow to follow hips
Both hands reach behind their back
trap: Free hand wide, trapped arm extended

flashcards.question: Roll from Chill Dog (top): What does their head-side grip change actually signal?
flashcards.answer: The arm moving around your head indicates the Chill Dog checkpoint, not proof that either player has a rear ride.

plausible: Arm trap opens as head grip changes
High leg lowers to ordinary guard
trap: Wrist pummel begins under your hand

flashcards.question: Roll from Chill Dog (top): Which free-leg movement can deepen the clinch?
flashcards.answer: A second leg joining behind the head reinforces the upper-body enclosure; maintain early inside space to prevent it.
flashcards.answer_line: Its closure high behind your head

plausible: The leg lowering toward the mat
Knee returns between the two chests
trap: Free foot settles low against hip

flashcards.question: Roll from Chill Dog (top): When is a backward elbow withdrawal appropriate?
flashcards.answer: Recover the elbow toward the ribs only through an opened high-leg connection rather than pulling against a fixed shoulder.

plausible: As soon as their free leg shifts
Whenever you can post the other hand
trap: Wrist moves; knee hug holds elbow

flashcards.question: Roll from Chill Dog (top): What should precede lifting your head after their reset?
flashcards.answer: Recover posture after the high leg and arm trap open; a change of direction alone does not establish clearance.

plausible: Only their hand touching the mat
Only your hips turning away
trap: Only second leg leaves upper back
